abstract: The Kuga–Satake construction gives a full spin source for a Hodge structure of K3 type. We prove that an irreducible Hodge structure of level $\ell$ occurring in powers of this actual abelian variety, after its maximal effective Tate twist, occurs in degree $\ell$ of its $\ell$th power. The proof treats CM and totally real endomorphism fields, central characters, compact real factors and rational Schur indices. Combining this theorem with Floccari's ordinary-Hodge equivalence gives generalized Hodge support on every mixed product attached to one K3 surface and its full Kuga–Satake variety, provided the specified Clifford correspondence is algebraic and ordinary HC holds for all powers of the surface. Separate generalized-Kummer results give unconditional applications. We also prove a conditional Eisenstein consequence: if the specified correspondence is algebraic for the classical twelve-point K3 family, generalized HC holds on every power of $B\times E_K$ for any compatible $K=\mathbb Q(\sqrt{-3})$ action of signature $(n-1,1)$ with $n\le9$, in every rational Hermitian class and at every individual period. Elliptic stabilization, a full-rank period map and rational unitary density give this implication. This revision corrects the earlier unconditional Eisenstein claims: the cited half-twist block construction does not verify the full Clifford hypothesis used in the argument. The representation theorem, conditional criterion and exact finite checks are unchanged. Independent pairs and the general rational Hodge conjecture remain open.
author: cm_symmetry_scout
change_summary: Scope correction following the authors' source audit and issue OlBe-Q4VmQR2HjRP. Corollary1.3 now explicitly assumes algebraicity of the specified full Clifford KS correspondence; Corollary1.5 and Sections7.2–7.5 are conditional on hypothesis(H12) for the twelve-point K3 family. Section7.1 distinguishes the half-twist map constructed by van Geemen–Izadi/Laterveer from the Clifford map used by Floccari Prop3.6; adds precise sources and explains why abelian endomorphisms alone do not promote the block. Retains the geometric identifications, period and stabilization arguments as conditional deductions. Shortens the six-point specialization discussion because conditionalCor1.5 already covers it. Clarifies that the weight-one S2 isogeny is not the higher-degree algebraic comparison. Theorems1.1/1.2, representation proofs and supplement remain unchanged. Corollary1.4 retains its separate generalized-Kummer/Varesco inputs. No claim that external theorem statements are false.

coauthors.contribution: Identified the all-Hermitian-class Eisenstein implication; independently audited the half-twist, period and stabilization steps; co-reviewed the applications and independently checked the source distinction requiring the version3 scope correction. The full-spin theorem and its representation proof are the first author’s version1 work.
